sections.html: Ancistrus chagresi Eigenmann & Eigenmann, 1889. Common name: Bristlenose Catfish. Size: 195 mm SL. pH 6.5–7.5; temperature 24–27°C. IUCN: Least Concern.
South America: Panama, Caribbean rivers, Chagres and Gatun. Type locality: Río Chagres, Panama Canal Zone, Panama. Habitat: Rio Ipeti, Panama.

Ancistrus should be fed mainly on vegetarian foods. Prepared foods include algae wafers and spirulina based sinking food. Vegetables such as courgette/zucchini and (English) cucumber are an excellent addition to the diet, along with the odd, small amount of more meaty foods.

A good complement to most aquariums, they are not aggressive to other species. Males may fight over territory if kept in too small a tank. Suitable with most community fish that aren't overly big or aggressive.

Mature males and sometimes females have soft tentacles (bushy fleshy growths) on the snout, which is unique to the genus Ancistrus. Males develop soft tentacles on the head; females sometimes do too, but never to the extent seen in males.
All Ancistrus species are cave-breeders, where the male looks after the eggs and young fry. There is no breeding report for this species.
